directAnswer: Pope Boniface V, a native of Naples, reigned from 619 to 625. He issued decrees on church asylum and the handling of relics, and, as Bede records, he supported the mission to the English, writing to King Edwin of Northumbria and granting the pallium to Archbishop Justus of Canterbury.

sections.h2: A Neapolitan Pope and His Decrees
paras: Boniface was born in Naples, the son of a man named John. After the death of Adeodatus I, more than a year passed before his consecration in December 619, during a period of unrest in Italy that included a revolt by the exarch Eleutherius. The Liber Pontificalis credits Boniface with decrees confirming the right of asylum in churches and ruling that acolytes were not to take the place of deacons in transferring the relics of martyrs. It also describes him as a gentle man who loved the clergy.

Boniface's best-documented work concerns England, through letters that Bede copied into his Ecclesiastical History. He sent the pallium to Justus, archbishop of Canterbury, with authority to consecrate bishops. He also wrote to King Edwin of Northumbria, urging him to accept Christianity, and to Edwin's Christian queen Æthelburh of Kent, encouraging her to work for her husband's conversion. Edwin was baptized in 627, after Boniface's death.
Boniface died on 25 October 625 and was buried in St. Peter's. Apart from these records, little is known about him.

keyFacts: Issued decrees on church asylum and the translation of relics
Granted the pallium to Justus of Canterbury
Wrote to King Edwin of Northumbria and Queen Æthelburh, as recorded by Bede

faqs.question: What was Boniface V's role in the conversion of England?
faqs.answer: He supported the Canterbury mission by granting the pallium to Archbishop Justus and wrote to King Edwin of Northumbria and his queen urging the king's conversion. Edwin was baptized in 627, two years after Boniface died.

faqs.question: What is the right of asylum that Boniface V confirmed?
faqs.answer: It was the custom that a person fleeing danger or punishment could take refuge in a church and could not be removed by force. The Liber Pontificalis says Boniface V issued a decree upholding it.
